Main.sentence: Drone warfare is a form of ___E:warfare U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warfare)___ using ___E:military drones U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_drone)___ or ___E:military robots U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_robot)___ .

The robots may be ___E:remote controlled U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telerobotics)___ by a pilot or have varying levels of ___E:autonomy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autonomous_robot)___ during their mission.

Types of robots include ___E:unmanned combat aerial vehicles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unmanned_combat_aerial_vehicle)___ (UCAV) or weaponized commercial ___E:unmanned aerial vehicles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unmanned_aerial_vehicle)___ (UAV), ___E:unmanned surface vehicles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unmanned_surface_vehicle)___ (USV) or ___E:unmanned underwater vehicles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unmanned_underwater_vehicle)___ (UUV), and ___E:unmanned ground vehicles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unmanned_ground_vehicle)___ (UGV).

UAVs, UGVs, USVs and UUVs are variously used for reconnaissance, kamikaze missions, bomb disposal, transporting cargo and ___E:medical evacuation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_evacuation)___ or may serve an ___E:anti-air U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-aircraft_warfare)___ , ___E:anti-armor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-tank_warfare)___ or ___E:anti-personnel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-personnel_weapon)___ role.  ___E:China U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unmanned_aerial_vehicles_of_China)___ , ___E:France U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unmanned_aerial_vehicles_in_the_French_Armed_Forces)___ , ___E:Greece U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unmanned_aerial_vehicles_in_the_Hellenic_Armed_Forces)___ , ___E:India U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India)___ , ___E:Iran U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran)___ , ___E:Iraq U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq)___ , ___E:Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israel)___ , ___E:Italy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy)___ , ___E:Pakistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan)___ , ___E:Poland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poland)___ , ___E:Russia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia)___ , ___E:South Korea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korea)___ , ___E:Turkey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey)___ , the ___E:United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States)___ , the ___E:United Kingdom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom)___ and ___E:Ukraine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukraine)___    are known to have manufactured operational UCAVs as of 2019.

Drones can be used for ___E:electronic warfare U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_warfare)___ , ___E:explosive ordnance disposal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Explosive_ordnance_disposal)___ , ___E:target training U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Target_drone)___ and augmenting logistics but are most commonly utilized for intelligence, surveillance, target acquisition, and reconnaissance ( ___E:ISTAR U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unmanned_surveillance_and_reconnaissance_aerial_vehicle)___ ), facilitating direct attacks on ___E:target U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Targeting_(warfare))___ as part of a ___E:kill chain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kill_chain_(military))___ or ___E:manned-unmanned teaming U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manned-unmanned_teaming)___ .

Aerial drone attacks can be conducted via purpose-built UCAVs deploying ___E:ordnance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_ordnance)___ during a drone strike or by weaponized commercial UAVs ___E:aerial dropping U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top-attack)___ munitions or ___E:crashing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loitering_munition)___ into a target.
Heavy-lift drones may also be used to ___E:airlift U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Airlift)___ supplies or transport wounded personnel across a battlefield.

Smaller drones such as ___E:SUAVs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miniature_UAV)___ and ___E:MAVs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Micro_air_vehicle)___ are man-portable and can be deployed for low-altitude, short-range support operations.

Larger drones can serve a "mothership" role by deploying smaller, sub-drones or by being equipped with electronic warfare features such as a ___E:signal repeater U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Repeater)___ .

Multiple drones may operate and attack simultaneously in a ___E:drone swarm U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swarm_robotics)___  and autonomous drones, such as ___E:LAWs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lethal_autonomous_weapon)___ , utilize ___E:military AI U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_applications_of_artificial_intelligence)___ .

The early years of the 21st century saw most drone strikes being ___E:conducted U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battlefield_UAVs_of_the_United_States)___ by the US military using ___E:air-to-surface missiles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air-to-surface_missile)___ against ground targets within countries such as ___E:Afghanistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_drone_strikes_in_Afghanistan)___ , ___E:Libya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_intervention_in_Libya_(2015%E2%80%932019))___ , ___E:Pakistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drone_strikes_in_Pakistan)___ , ___E:Somalia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_intervention_in_Somalia_(2007%E2%80%93present))___ , ___E:Syria U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_intervention_in_the_Syrian_civil_war)___ , and ___E:Yemen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_airstrikes_on_Yemen)___ during the ___E:war on terror U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_on_terror)___ .

Drone warfare evolved and proliferated quickly in the 2010s and 2020s, with countries such as ___E:Azerbaijan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azerbaijan)___  , China, ___E:Iran U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unmanned_aerial_vehicles_in_the_Iranian_military)___ , Russia, Turkey and Ukraine utilizing drones with increased ubiquity.

Militant groups, such as the ___E:Islamic State U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_State)___ and ___E:Houthis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houthi)___ , and ___E:organized crime U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organized_crime)___ groups such as ___E:Mexican cartels U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_cartels)___ likewise utilized drones for attacks against adversaries and for logistical purposes.

Since 2022, drone warfare has been extensively used in the ___E:Russian invasion of Ukraine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine)___ by both sides, including long range fixed-wing drones, and short range multirotor ___E:FPV drones U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FPV_drone)___ .

Scholars have described the conflict as the first "drone war", due to the large scale and high intensity of attacks, and agree on the major role drone warfare has in ___E:modern U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_warfare)___ ___E:conventional warfare U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conventional_warfare)___ .

A commercial UCAV is any commercially-produced UAV that is modified to carry such weapons as ___E:guided bombs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guided_bomb)___ , ___E:cluster bombs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cluster_bomb)___ , ___E:incendiary devices U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incendiary_device)___ , ___E:air-to-surface missiles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air-to-surface_missile)___ , ___E:air-to-air missiles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air-to-air_missile)___ , ___E:anti-tank guided missiles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-tank_guided_missile)___ or other types of ___E:precision-guided munitions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Precision-guided_munition)___ , ___E:autocannons U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autocannon)___ and ___E:machine guns U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Machine_gun)___ .
These weaponized civilian drones may proceed to fire munition or a missile, drop explosives and crash into or ___E:detonate above U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_burst)___ vulnerable targets.

Payloads could include explosives such as ___E:hand grenades U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hand_grenade)___ , ___E:mortar U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mortar_(weapon))___ ___E:shells U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shell_(projectile))___ and ___E:IEDs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Improvised_explosive_device)___ or other dangerous materials such as shrapnel, chemical, radiological or biological hazards.

These relatively cheap drones are also used for non-attack roles. ___E:Multirotor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multirotor)___ FPV drones have been used extensively by both armies for ___E:aerial reconnaissance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aerial_reconnaissance)___ and ___E:artillery spotting U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artillery_spotting)___ in the ___E:Russo-Ukraine War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russo-Ukraine_War)___ .
___E:Anti-UAV systems U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-aircraft_warfare#Anti-UAV_defenses)___ are being developed by states to counter the threat posed by commercial UCAVs.

According to James Rogers, an academic who studies drone warfare, "There is a big debate out there at the moment about what the best way is to counter these small UAVs, whether they are used by ___E:hobbyists U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hobbyist)___ causing a bit of a nuisance or in a more sinister manner by a ___E:terrorist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrorist)___ actor."

Estimates for the total number of people killed in U.S. ___E:drone strikes in Pakistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drone_strikes_in_Pakistan)___ range from 2,000 to 3,500 militants killed and 158 to 965 civilians killed.   81 insurgent leaders in Pakistan have been killed.  ___E:Drone strikes in Yemen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drone_strikes_in_Yemen)___ are estimated to have killed 846–1,758 militants and 116–225 civilians.   57 ___E:Al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Qaeda_in_the_Arabian_Peninsula)___ leaders are confirmed to have been killed.

In August 2018, Al Jazeera reported that a ___E:Saudi Arabian-led coalition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Arabian-led_intervention_in_Yemen)___ combating Houthi rebels in Yemen had secured secret deals with ___E:al-Qaeda in Yemen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Qaeda_in_the_Arabian_Peninsula)___ and recruited hundreds of that group's fighters: "...
Key figures in the deal-making said the United States was aware of the arrangements and held off on drone attacks against the armed group, which was created by Osama bin Laden in 1988."

After US president ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ had increased drone strikes by over 400%,    his successor ___E:Joe Biden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden)___ reversed course.
Under Biden, drone strikes reportedly decreased.

A ___E:Biden administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_Joe_Biden)___ ___E:drone strike U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/August_2021_Kabul_drone_strike)___ in ___E:Kabul U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabul)___ , Afghanistan in August 2021 killed 10 civilians, including seven children.
Later, a drone strike killed ___E:Al-Qaeda U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Qaeda)___ leader ___E:Ayman al-Zawahiri U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ayman_al-Zawahiri)___ .

By mid-2025, reports emerged that the U.S. military was lagging behind in evolving its drone warfare capabilities, particularly its production and deployment of small, low-cost first-person view UAVs akin to those seen during the ___E:Russian invasion of Ukraine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine)___ .
A July 2025 memo by defense secretary ___E:Pete Hegseth U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_Hegseth)___ urged military leadership to accelerate the adoption of drones among troops.

In September 2025 the U.S. envoy to ___E:Ukraine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukraine)___ , ___E:Keith Kellogg U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Kellogg)___ , stated Ukraine had overtaken the U.S. in drone technology amid the Russo-Ukrainian war, as battlefield experience prompted continuous innovation in drones.

Defense industry executive Steve Siomi, the president of robotics defense company ___E:Allen Control Systems U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Allen_Control_Systems&action=edit&redlink=1)___ , said China had overtaken the U.S. in responding to drone proliferation and argued that drone adoption made warfare more affordable for all combatants, including America's rivals.
Scholarly opinions are mixed regarding the efficacy of drone strikes.

Some studies support that ___E:decapitation strikes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decapitation_strike)___ to kill a terrorist or insurgent group's leadership limits the capabilities of these groups in the future, while other studies contradict this. Drone strikes are successful at suppressing militant behavior, though this response is in anticipation of a drone strike rather than as a result of one. Data from the US and Pakistan's joint counter-terrorism efforts show that militants cease communication and attack planning to avoid detection and targeting.
Proponents of drone strikes assert that drone strikes are largely effective in targeting specific combatants.

Some scholars argue that drone strikes reduce the amount of ___E:civilian casualties U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civilian_casualties_from_U.S._drone_strikes)___ and territorial damage when compared to other types of military force like large bombs.
Military alternatives to drone strikes, such as raids and interrogations, can be extremely risky, time-consuming, and potentially ineffective.

Relying on drone strikes does not come without risks as U.S. drone usage sets an international precedent on ___E:extraterritorial U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extraterritorial_operation)___ and ___E:extrajudicial U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extrajudicial_killing)___ killings.
In Mexico, ___E:Drug cartel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drug_cartel)___ drone operators are called "droneros" who are known to use bomb-dropping drones on enemy targets.

___E:UCAVs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unmanned_combat_aerial_vehicle)___ were used extensively by the ___E:Azerbaijani Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azerbaijani_Armed_Forces)___ against the ___E:Armenian Army U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armed_Forces_of_Armenia)___ during the ___E:2020 Nagorno-Karabakh conflict U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Nagorno-Karabakh_conflict)___ .

These UCAVs included Israeli ___E:IAI Harops U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IAI_Harop)___ and Turkish ___E:Bayraktar TB2s. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bayraktar_TB2)___  As the Bayraktar TB2 utilizes ___E:Canadian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada)___ optics and laser targeting systems, Canada suspended export of its military drone technology to Turkey in October 2020 after allegations that the technology had been used to collect intelligence and direct artillery and missile fire at military positions.
After the incident, ___E:Aselsan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aselsan)___ stated that it would begin the serial production and integration of the CATS system to replace the Canadian MX15B.

The Economist has cited ___E:Azerbaijan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azerbaijan)___ 's highly effective use of drones against Armenia in the ___E:2020 Nagorno-Karabakh war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Nagorno-Karabakh_war)___ and ___E:Turkey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkey)___ 's use of drones in the ___E:Syrian Civil War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrian_Civil_War)___ as indicating the future of warfare.

Noting that it had previously been assumed that drones would not play a major role in conflicts between nations due to their vulnerability to anti-aircraft fire, it suggested that while this might be true for major powers with air defenses, it was less true for minor powers.
It noted Azerbaijani tactics and Turkey's use of drones as indicating a "new, more affordable type of ___E:air power U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_power)___ ".
It also noted that the ability of drones to record their kills enabled a highly effective Azerbaijani propaganda campaign.

On 24 July 2025, the ___E:Royal Thai Armed Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Thai_Armed_Forces)___ launched coordinated drone strikes against the ___E:Royal Cambodian Armed Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Cambodian_Armed_Forces)___ in the disputed border area near ___E:Ta Muen Thom U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prasat_Ta_Muen_Thom)___ and ___E:Ta Krabey U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ta_Krabey)___ .
Using FPV drones, quadcopters, and one-way kamikaze UAVs, Thai forces targeted Cambodian command posts, ammunition depots, artillery positions, and communication lines.

Analysts described the campaign as one of the most prominent uses of commercial multirotor drones in a state-on-state conflict since the war in Ukraine, challenging assumptions that such drones are ineffective in dense jungle terrain.

On 9 September 2025, over a dozen allegedly Russian drones ___E:breached Polish airspace U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Russian_drone_incursion_into_Poland)___ , prompting a NATO ___E:Quick Reaction Alert U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quick_Reaction_Alert)___ and Poland invoking ___E:Article 4 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Atlantic_Treaty#Article_4)___ of the NATO treaty.

At least four of the drones were confirmed shot down. On 18 September Polish and ___E:Ukrainian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukraine)___ officials announced that the two countries would establish joint military training and production programs, as the Ukrainian military had emerged as a major pioneer in drone warfare in the years following the ___E:2022 Russian invasion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine)___ .

During the ___E:Russo-Ukrainian war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russo-Ukrainian_war_(2022%E2%80%93present))___ , both sides used drones in combat and for reconnaissance, and drones played an important role in long-range bombing attacks and supporting ground assaults and offensives.
Ukrainian forces extensively used the Turkish-made ___E:Bayraktar TB2 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baykar_Bayraktar_TB2)___ drone throughout the conflict in strikes against Russian forces.

Russian forces meanwhile launched waves of Iranian ___E:HESA Shahed 136 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HESA_Shahed_136)___ drones during the ___E:October 2022 missile strikes on Ukraine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October_2022_missile_strikes_on_Ukraine)___ .
The main roles of drones in the war, however, are in reconnaissance and ___E:artillery spotting U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artillery_spotting)___ .
Russian sources claimed to have used a "Stupor anti-drone rifle" to jam the radio controls of Ukrainian drones.
On 13 October 2022, the first recorded instance of an unarmed drone-on-drone combat encounter occurred above the ___E:Donetsk U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donetsk)___ region of Ukraine.

A Ukrainian ___E:DJI Mavic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DJI_Mavic)___ quadcopter was recorded ramming a Russian drone of the same model, resulting in the latter crashing towards the surface below.

Another instance of this aerial ramming tactic occurred on 24 November 2022, this time with the Russian DJI Mavic being recorded plummeting towards the ground after a collision with a Ukrainian drone.
On 9 May 2023, a Russian conscript surrendered to (or rather via) a Ukrainian drone.
The average HESA Shahed 136 drone is worth about $20,000. An ___E:IRIS-T U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IRIS-T)___ missile is worth about $430,000 each in comparison.
From 13 September until 17 October, open source information suggests that Ukraine has had to spend $28.14 million on defending against these drones.

Since at least September 2022, Ukraine has used black ___E:naval drones U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unmanned_surface_vehicle)___ , equipped with the ___E:Starlink U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starlink_in_the_Russo-Ukrainian_War)___ satellite internet system, to carry attacks on the Russian ___E:Black Sea fleet U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Sea_Fleet)___ at the ___E:Sevastopol Naval base U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevastopol_Naval_Base)___ .

The naval drones were at first assumed to be for reconnaissance, but appear to carry munitions and act as a bomb.  With experts noting that the sensors on the front of the naval drone could be used as a ___E:laser range finder U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laser_rangefinder)___ to help in targeting.

In late October 2022, seven of these drones were used to mount a ___E:successful drone attack U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_drone_attack_on_the_Sevastopol_Naval_Base)___ on the Sevastopol Naval base.
On 13 October 2022, a Ukrainian ___E:MiG-29 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikoyan_MiG-29)___ became the first manned plane to go down during combat due to a drone.
The pilot is claimed to have destroyed a ___E:Shahed-136 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shahed-136)___ drone with his cannon.
The blast is believed to have brought the plane down and hospitalised the pilot.
In September 2023, Ukrainian troops were reportedly using cardboard drones with GoPro cameras for aerial reconnaissance.

Since the 2022 ___E:Russian invasion of Ukraine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine)___ , approximately 30 companies in Ukraine have emerged to mass-produce drones for the war effort.

The ___E:Ukraine government U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_Ukraine)___ Ministry of Digital Transformation initiated the "Army of Drones" project and attempted to purchase up to 200,000 drones in 2023, aiming to deploy relatively cheap drones against large advantages Russia has had in military equipment.

In 2023, they also sponsored several competitions where the "dozens of drone developers that have sprung up all over Ukraine" are invited to make simulated attacks on ground targets, or chase ___E:fixed-wing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fixed-wing_aircraft)___ drones, or even participate in drone ___E:dogfight U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dogfight)___ competitions.
One new model that has been successful is the " ___E:Baba Yaga U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baba_Yaga_(aircraft))___ " hexacopter, which can carry "44 pounds of payload".

As of April 2024, Ukraine has started deploying manned aircraft, such as the ___E:Aeroprakt A-22 Foxbat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aeroprakt_A-22_Foxbat)___ and ___E:Yakovlev Yak-52 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yakovlev_Yak-52)___ , which uses snipers or machine guns to shoot down Russian drones.

Ukrainian drones have also been given a variety of improvised modifications for the express purpose of attacking and countering Russian drones; these include an instance in July 2024 where an FPV drone with a stick mounted to it was used to attack and eventually destroy a ___E:ZALA 421-16E U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ZALA_Aero_Group)___ reconnaissance drone through repeated ___E:aerial ramming U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aerial_ramming)___ .
In 2024 ___E:drones controlled a through a tether with optical fiber U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiber_optic_drone)___ became commonplace, thus avoiding radio jamming.

On 31 July 2024, a Russian ___E:Mi-8 helicopter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mil_Mi-28)___ was shot down over occupied Donetsk, by a Ukrainian FPV drone, the first time a helicopter in combat was destroyed by a drone.
The Mi-8 was believed to have been attacked on the ground either during landing or take off.
Russia launched the largest drone strike of the war on 25 November 2024, when it attacked Ukraine with 188 drones.
Ukrainian forces shot down 76 and lost track of 96, likely due to electronic jamming.
Other drones ___E:struck the energy grid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_strikes_against_Ukrainian_infrastructure_(2022%E2%80%93present))___ and civilian homes.
On 8 February 2025, Russian authorities reportedly discovered a plot in which a shipment of FPV drone headsets loaded with explosives were sent to Russian soldiers.
Each headset had 10-15 grams of explosives and were programmed to detonate on activation.
Officials compared it to the ___E:2024 Lebanon electronic device attacks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Lebanon_electronic_device_attacks)___ by Israel.
Subsequent reports claimed 8 Russian FPV pilots lost their eyesight due to explosions between 4 and 7 February.
The first explosion was reported on 4 February in the Belgorod oblast, subsequent explosions occurred in Kursk, Luhansk and Donetsk regions.

The largest drone-and‑missile attack by Russia since the full‑scale invasion occurred on 18–25 May 2025, during which Russian forces launched approximately 1,000 aerial weapons against Ukraine, combining 355 Shahed drones, about 23 Iskander ballistic missiles, and over 60 air‑launched cruise missiles, including the X‑101 and X‑555. The assault hit Kyiv and multiple other regions, killing more than 15 civilians and injuring dozens, while dramatically increasing pressure on Ukraine’s air defenses and supply chains

On 1 June 2025, Ukrainian FPV drones smuggled into Russia were launched from trucks to ___E:strike Russian airbases U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Spiderweb)___ , including ___E:Belaya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belaya_air_base)___ and ___E:Olenya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olenya_airbase)___ , destroying multiple Russian strategic bombers.
Starting in August 2025, Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian oil refineries have caused a ___E:fuel crisis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Russian_fuel_crisis)___ in Russia.

In June 2025, as part of the ___E:2025 Iran-Israel War U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran%E2%80%93Israel_War)___ , Iran launched several drone attacks on Israel in response to Israel's bombing of Iranian nuclear facilities.

In 2020, a ___E:Turkish-made UAV U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STM_Kargu)___ loaded with explosives detected and attacked ___E:Haftar's forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libyan_National_Army)___ in ___E:Libya U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libya)___ with ___E:artificial intelligence U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence)___ and without command, according to a report from the ___E:UN Security Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UN_Security_Council)___ 's Panel of Experts on Libya published in March 2021. It was considered the first attack carried out by an AI UAV.

On 19 September 2025, amid the ___E:siege of El Fasher U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siege_of_El_Fasher)___ during the ___E:Sudanese civil war U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudanese_civil_war_(2023%E2%80%93present))___ , a ___E:Rapid Support Forces U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapid_Support_Forces)___ drone struck a mosque at an ___E:IDP U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internally_displaced_person)___ camp, killing 75 people.

On 6 January 2018, Russian forces thwarted a ___E:drone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unmanned_aerial_vehicle)___ (UAV) swarm attack on the ___E:Khmeimim Air Base U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khmeimim_Air_Base)___ , the first of this kind in the history of warfare.

On 7 October 2023, ___E:Hamas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamas)___ launched ___E:incursions of southern Israel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October_7_attacks)___ , using commercial drones to bomb Israeli guard towers before breaching the ___E:border wall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza%E2%80%93Israel_barrier)___ .
Videos of Israeli troops and a ___E:Merkava IV U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merkava_IV)___ tank being taken out by drones surfaced on the internet.
